description: Lots of very small e-commerce charges hitting one card in quick succession, usually under five dollars, at different shops.
Stolen card numbers being validated with a rapid series of micro-transactions online.
Account takeover: an expensive online order from a device we have never seen, far bigger than what the customer normally spends.
Online purchases over $500 from an unfamiliar device where the IP address is in a different country from where the cardholder lives.
Recently opened accounts that suddenly rack up thousands of dollars of spending in a single day.
Synthetic identities: accounts less than a month old buying gift cards or electronics in large amounts.
Card used in person in a foreign country only a few hours after it was used at home - physically impossible travel.
Skimmed cards being cashed out at ATMs abroad, with transactions in more than one country on the same day.
High-value crypto purchases or gambling deposits made between 1am and 4am.
Large gambling or crypto transactions over $800 in the early hours of the morning.
Unusual velocity: more than 10 transactions on one card within 24 hours totalling over $3000.
Flag any transaction where the customer's credit score is below 500 and they have more than 3 chargebacks.
Just flag the transactions that are labelled as fraud, i.e. where is_fraud is true.
